stories.title: A brain implant let a woman with ALS sing a musical scale again
stories.summary: UC Davis turned a 58-year-old trained singer's attempts to sing into a synthetic voice that changes pitch, using 384 electrodes in her brain's speech area; she could sound happy, ask a question and sing a scale. Early-trial results presented at Neuroscience 2026, not yet in a journal.

predictions.note: A 384-electrode implant turned a woman's attempts to sing into a voice that changes pitch; early-trial results presented at a conference, not yet in a journal.

stories.title: Gene editing is giving a Melbourne man the immune system he was born without
stories.summary: Matthew Rozek, 29, born with SCID ('bubble boy disease'), had his own stem cells gene-edited at the US National Institutes of Health; he has gained 10 kg and his immune system is improving. One patient in an early trial; WEHI in Melbourne is working on a simpler injectable version.

stories.title: A locked-in man communicated by implant for over a year, and brain-to-text ran on an iPhone
stories.summary: At Neuroscience 2026, a Mass General team reported a completely locked-in person communicating independently for more than a year with a brain implant, and Emory and Georgia Tech showed a portable brain-to-text system that runs even on an iPhone. Early-trial conference reports.

predictions.note: A completely locked-in person communicated independently for more than a year through a brain implant, in an early trial reported at Neuroscience 2026.

stories.title: A Doctor Octopus-inspired brain cap picks commands for extra robot arms while your hands keep working
stories.summary: Imperial College London's non-invasive cap reads the brain's response to buzzes on the arm to pick one of four commands; after three days, 10 volunteers got it right about 70% of the time while balancing a tray with both hands. A small lab study.

predictions.note: A non-invasive EEG cap let 10 volunteers pick commands for extra robot arms about 70% of the time while both hands stayed busy, in a small lab study.

stories.title: OpenAI's ChatGPT Wallet lets its AI agents shop for you
stories.summary: OpenAI's Dots agents can now buy things with a card stored in ChatGPT Wallet, checking with you and asking for Face ID or a fingerprint before every purchase; the card becomes a payment token the agent never sees. A product launch; some shops still block agents.

stories.title: Penn built soft robot muscles that tap piano keys gently or firmly and hold a steady gaze
stories.summary: University of Pennsylvania engineers made artificial muscle fibres from a liquid crystal elastomer, graphene and a copper coil that both heats and senses, modelled on the small muscles of our eyes and fingers. A lab prototype.

stories.title: One gene-editing infusion kept blood fats lower in monkeys for three years
stories.summary: A CRISPR base editor that switches off the liver gene ANGPTL3 kept triglycerides 43% lower (LDL 13% lower) in 10 monkeys for three years. A company-funded monkey study from Verve Therapeutics, part of Eli Lilly; a human version is in an early trial.

stories.title: Alzheimer's shrinks two brain areas up to a decade before symptoms, Johns Hopkins scans show
stories.summary: Hundreds of MRI and PET scans showed the entorhinal cortex and amygdala losing tissue earlier than the hippocampus, with changes as much as a decade before symptoms. An imaging study of group trends that could point to a window for treating sooner.

stories.title: Diet with exercise, and drugs like metformin, turned ageing clocks back; most supplements didn't
stories.summary: Yale pooled 51 studies and more than 110 DNA-methylation markers: diet plus exercise, metformin, semaglutide and anti-TNF drugs lowered epigenetic age, while over-the-counter supplements didn't measurably. Changes in these clocks don't yet prove longer lives.

stories.title: The brain's deep-sleep rinse runs weaker in older adults, MIT found
stories.summary: Scanning younger (18-39) and older (60-84) volunteers as they slept in an MRI, MIT found the waves of fluid that help clear the brain in deep sleep were much smaller in older adults, tied to fewer slow brain waves. Whether that raises dementia risk is the next question.
stories.evidence: Imaging study, younger vs older adults

stories.title: Australia's GPs now have backing to prescribe time in nature
stories.summary: The Royal Australian College of GPs has endorsed resources for recommending 20 minutes a day noticing nature; a review of 47 trials with almost 3,800 people found mental-health gains in 17 of them. Whether a GP's prescription itself makes the difference is still being studied.

stories.title: Pitching basic income as fairness lifted support among Americans who value equality
stories.summary: In a survey experiment with 2,024 US adults, people's values mattered more than their party: framing a universal basic income as fairness raised support among those who value equality, but backfired with those who oppose it. Modest shifts from a single survey.

stories.title: Blood NAD, which longevity supplements try to boost, didn't drop with age in healthy adults
stories.summary: In 1,068 adults, whole-blood NAD held steady with age in healthy people but was lower in those with heart disease, especially high blood pressure. An observational study of blood only; it says nothing yet about whether supplements help.

stories.title: Neuroscientists proposed eight tests for whether lab-grown mini brains could become conscious
stories.summary: Lucia Melloni and Stanislas Dehaene set out electrical-stimulation tests, such as whether the tissue notices a missing expected signal; Melloni doesn't think today's organoids are conscious and backs an international board to oversee the research. A proposal, with no experiment yet.

stories.title: SpaceX caught a Starship back from orbit for the first time, though its booster was lost
stories.summary: Ship 42 settled into the launch tower's arms in Texas about 22.5 hours after Flight 15 lifted off, a first for Starship's upper stage and a big step toward a fully reusable rocket. The Super Heavy booster aborted its own catch and was lost in the Gulf of Mexico.

stories.title: Socks that stiffen the arch cut the energy cost of walking by 2%
stories.summary: UT Austin's knitted band around the ball of the foot stiffened the arch by 65% and cut 12 young adults' energy use while walking by 2%, about like taking a 2 kg weight off the waist. A small lab study.

stories.title: Floaty, a kestrel-inspired robot, rides updrafts like a bird to save battery
stories.summary: Max Planck and University of Stuttgart researchers built a flying robot that adjusts four wing flaps to hold its place in rising air, steady in wind-tunnel gusts up to 10 m/s. Early wind-tunnel tests.

transcript.t: It's Monday, November 16, and this is the Transhuman Daily.
Here's your day in transhumanism, in 3 minutes flat.
The weekend's best is about second chances.
Through a brain implant, a woman with ALS sang again.
And gene editing is giving a Melbourne m an the immune system he was born without.
A locked-in man communicated by implant for over a year, and brain-to-text even ran on an iPhone.
Imperial took a cue from Doctor Octopus: a brain cap for extra robot arms, while your hands keep working.
OpenAI's new ChatGPT Wallet lets its AI agents shop for you, checking with you before every purchase.
And Penn built soft robot muscles that tap piano keys gently or firmly, and hold a steady gaze.
On to longevity. In monkeys, a single gene-editing infusion kept blood fats lower for three years.
And Johns Hopkins scans show Alzheimer's shrinks t wo brain areas up to a decade before memory slips.
Yale found diet with exercise, and drugs like metformin, turned ageing clocks back. Most supplements didn't.
And MIT found the brain's deep-sleep rinse runs weaker in older adults.
On to wellbeing.
Australia's GPs now have backing to prescribe time in nature, 20 minutes a day.
And a US survey found pitching basic income as fair ness lifted support among people who value equality.
Now, the catch. Blood NAD, which longevity supplements try to boost, didn't drop with age in healthy adults.
And just in case, neuroscientists proposed eight tests for whether lab-grown mini brains could become conscious.
SpaceX caught a Starship back from orbit for the first time, though its booster was lost.
Back on the ground, socks that stiffen the arch cut the energy cost of walking by 2%.
Oh, and Floaty, a kestrel-inspired robot, rides updrafts like a bird to save battery.
A voice back, a life back, a rocket home. The future's full of second chances.
Zoom out, and the line only goes up.
And the future keeps arriving ahead of schedule.
One day, all of this. Tomorrow, probably more.
You've been watching the Transhuman Daily.
Live long. See you tomorrow.
